Turkish · 1,000 words

Turkish words 501–600

Turkish words 501 to 600, by how often they're used, each with its meaning in English, an example sentence and, for verbs, the main forms (he, she or it). 64 of them are taught in the lessons of the course.

Learn them with spaced repetition, Anki-style: open the flashcards. Free, no account needed.

Overview1–100101–200201–300301–400401–500501–600601–700701–800801–900901–1000
  1. 501
    sevinmekverb

    to be glad, to be happy (about)

    Habere çok sevindim.

    I was really glad to hear the news.

    aorist sevinir · present seviniyor · past sevindi · future sevinecek

    What you're glad about takes the dative: Buna sevindim. Tanıştığımıza sevindim = Nice to meet you.

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 4: Verbal nouns

  2. 502
    deliadjective

    crazy, mad; madman (noun)

    Deli misin? Bu soğukta denize mi gireceksin?

    Are you crazy? You're going swimming in this cold?

    Colloquial, and rude about a person. Deli gibi = like crazy: deli gibi çalışmak.

    A2

  3. 503
    zararnoun

    harm, damage; loss

    Fırtına evlere çok zarar verdi.

    The storm did a lot of damage to the houses.

    Zarar vermek = to damage; Zararı yok = No harm done, it doesn't matter. The opposite of kâr (profit).

    B1

  4. 504
    askernoun

    soldier

    Kardeşim askerde, haziranda dönüyor.

    My brother is doing his military service; he's back in June.

    Askerde = doing military service; askere gitmek = to go into military service; askerlik = military service.

    A2

  5. 505
    ruhnoun

    soul, spirit; mind (ruh hâli: mood); ghost

    Bugün ruh hâlim çok iyi.

    I'm in a really good mood today.

    Ruh hâli = mood. Back-vowel suffixes: ruhu. A ghost is usually hayalet.

    B1

  6. 506
    içkinoun

    (alcoholic) drink; alcohol

    Teşekkürler, ben içki içmiyorum.

    Thanks, I don't drink.

    Only alcohol: a drink in general is içecek, a soft drink meşrubat.

    A2

  7. 507
    aitpostposition

    belonging to; about, concerning

    Bu çanta kime ait?

    Who does this bag belong to?

    After the dative: bana ait (mine). Formal; speech often says Bu çanta kimin?

    C1First taught in C1 · Unit 1: Stacked modality

  8. 508
    milyonnumber

    million

    İstanbul'da on beş milyondan fazla insan yaşıyor.

    More than fifteen million people live in Istanbul.

    Unlike yüz and bin, it takes bir: bir milyon.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 5: Formal Turkish

  9. 509
    kayıtnoun

    registration, record; recording

    Kayıt için kimliğinizi getirin.

    Bring your ID to register.

    accusative kaydı

    The ı drops and the t becomes d before a vowel: kaydı. Kaydolmak = to register, to sign up; kaydetmek = to save, to record.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 10: As long as, unless, in case

  10. 510
    patronnoun

    boss

    Patronum bugün çok sinirli.

    My boss is in a bad mood today.

    The boss or business owner, not a customer. A manager is müdür.

    A2

  11. 511
    fotoğrafnoun

    photo, photograph

    Bir fotoğrafımızı çeker misiniz?

    Could you take a photo of us?

    Fotoğraf çekmek = to take a photo; fotoğraf makinesi = camera.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 9: My family

  12. 512
    kolnoun

    arm; sleeve

    Düştüm ve kolumu kırdım.

    I fell and broke my arm.

    Also a sleeve: kısa kollu (short-sleeved). Kol saati = wristwatch.

    A1

  13. 513
    takmakverb

    to put on, to wear (glasses, jewellery, a belt); to attach, to fit

    Gözlüğünü tak, yoksa göremezsin.

    Put your glasses on or you won't see.

    aorist takar · present takıyor · past taktı · future takacak

    Accessories take takmak, clothes giymek. Casual: Takma kafana = Don't worry about it.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 6: Must and need

  14. 514
    normaladjective

    normal; ordinary, usual

    Bu çok normal, merak etme.

    That's perfectly normal, don't worry.

    Takes front-vowel suffixes: normalde (normally, usually).

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 4: Noun clauses

  15. 515
    asıladjective

    real, actual; main; original

    Asıl sorun bu değil.

    That's not the real problem.

    The ı drops before a vowel: aslı (the original). Aslında = actually, in fact.

    C1First taught in C1 · Unit 6: Word order and focus

  16. 516
    memnunadjective

    pleased, satisfied; glad

    Yeni işinden memnun musun?

    Are you happy with your new job?

    What you're pleased with takes the ablative. Memnun oldum = Nice to meet you.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 3: Saying who you are

  17. 517
    grupnoun

    group; band (music)

    Turistler büyük bir grupla geldi.

    The tourists came in a big group.

    accusative grubu

    The p becomes b before a vowel: grubu. Also a band: rock grubu.

    A2

  18. 518
    karışmakverb

    to mix, to get mixed up; to interfere, to meddle; to get confused

    Sen karışma, bu benim işim.

    Stay out of it, it's my business.

    aorist karışır · present karışıyor · past karıştı · future karışacak

    What you meddle in takes the dative: İşime karışma. Kafam karıştı = I'm confused.

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 12: Reported speech

  19. 519
    resimnoun

    picture, painting; drawing

    Çocuklar resim yapıyor.

    The children are drawing.

    accusative resmi

    The i drops before a vowel: resmi (the picture), not to be confused with resmî (official). Resim yapmak = to draw, to paint.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 2: Vowel harmony and plurals

  20. 520
    galibaadverb

    probably, I think; apparently

    Galiba yağmur yağacak.

    I think it's going to rain.

    A guess, like herhâlde. Often with -mIş: Galiba gitmiş (Looks like she's left).

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 2: Was, were, and once upon a time

  21. 521
    kısaadjective

    short

    Toplantı kısa sürdü.

    The meeting was short.

    For length and time; a short person is kısa boylu. The opposite is uzun. Kısaca = briefly.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 4: Questions and negation

  22. 522
    alointerjection

    hello (on the phone)

    Alo, Ayşe? Beni duyuyor musun?

    Hello, Ayşe? Can you hear me?

    Only on the phone. Answering a call, people also say Efendim?

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 5: Where things are

  23. 523
    tahminnoun

    guess; estimate; forecast

    Tahminim doğru çıktı.

    My guess turned out to be right.

    Tahmin etmek = to guess, to estimate; Tahmin et! = Guess! Hava tahmini = weather forecast.

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 9: Conditionals

  24. 524
    buluşmakverb

    to meet (up); to get together

    Yarın kafede buluşalım mı?

    Shall we meet at the café tomorrow?

    aorist buluşur · present buluşuyor · past buluştu · future buluşacak

    An arranged meeting, with ile: Ayşe'yle buluştum. To meet someone for the first time is tanışmak.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 7: Let's: suggestions and wishes

  25. 525
    seksnoun

    sex

    Bu dizide seks ve şiddet yok.

    There's no sex or violence in this series.

    A loanword, used much as in English; seksi = sexy. Not to be confused with seksen (eighty).

    B1

  26. 526
    çenenoun

    jaw, chin; talkativeness (çenesi düşük: chatty)

    Çenesi çok düşük, hiç susmuyor.

    She's a real chatterbox, she never stops talking.

    Çene çalmak = to chat. Çeneni kapa! = Shut up! (rude)

    B1

  27. 527
    kelimenoun

    word

    Bu kelimenin anlamı ne?

    What does this word mean?

    A single word. Söz is a word as something said, or a promise.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 2: Vowel harmony and plurals

  28. 528
    dersnoun

    lesson, class; subject (at school)

    Yarın sabah dokuzda dersim var.

    I have a class at nine tomorrow morning.

    Ders çalışmak = to study (for school); ders vermek = to teach.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 7: To and from

  29. 529
    taşımakverb

    to carry; to move (things)

    Bu valizi taşıyabilir misin?

    Can you carry this suitcase?

    aorist taşır · present taşıyor · past taşıdı · future taşıyacak

    Taşınmak = to move (house): Yeni bir eve taşındık.

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 5: The subject participle

  30. 530
    sokmakverb

    to put in, to insert; to let in; to sting, to bite (insects, snakes)

    Bir arı beni soktu.

    A bee stung me.

    aorist sokar · present sokuyor · past soktu · future sokacak

    The opposite of çıkarmak: Elini cebine soktu (He put his hand in his pocket). Not to be confused with sokak (street).

    B1

  31. 531
    eşnoun

    husband or wife, spouse; partner; the other one of a pair

    Eşim de öğretmen.

    My husband is a teacher too.

    Neutral for husband or wife. Also one of a pair: Bu çorabın eşi nerede? (Where's the other sock?)

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 9: My family

  32. 532
    patlamakverb

    to explode, to burst; to break out; to go flat (a tire)

    Lastik patladı, yolda kaldık.

    We had a flat tire and got stuck on the road.

    aorist patlar · present patlıyor · past patladı · future patlayacak

    The a becomes ı before -(I)yor: patlıyor. Patlamış mısır = popcorn.

    B1

  33. 533
    ilginoun

    interest; attention

    Tarihe büyük ilgisi var.

    She's very interested in history.

    What it concerns takes the dative. İlgilenmek = to be interested in, to look after; ilginç = interesting.

    B1

  34. 534
    hattaadverb

    even; in fact

    Herkes geldi, hatta Murat bile.

    Everyone came, even Murat.

    Adds something stronger, often with bile: hatta starts the phrase, bile follows the word.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 8: Small words: dA, bile, ki, ya

  35. 535
    ağıznoun

    mouth; accent, dialect

    Kapalı ağıza sinek girmez.

    A closed mouth catches no flies.

    accusative ağzı

    The ı drops before a vowel: ağzı, ağzım. Also a regional accent: Karadeniz ağzı. The example is a proverb.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 9: My family

  36. 536
    noktanoun

    point; dot, period (full stop); spot

    Cümlenin sonuna nokta koy.

    Put a period at the end of the sentence.

    The punctuation mark, and the dot in web addresses. Bu noktada = at this point.

    A2

  37. 537
    kralnoun

    king

    Masalda kralın üç kızı var.

    In the tale, the king has three daughters.

    Kraliçe = queen. Ottoman rulers are called padişah or sultan.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 3: Although, despite, without

  38. 538
    yakmakverb

    to burn; to light (a fire, a candle); to turn on (a light)

    Ateşi yaktık ve şarkı söyledik.

    We lit the fire and sang songs.

    aorist yakar · present yakıyor · past yaktı · future yakacak

    Also to turn on a light: ışığı yak. Yanmak = to burn (by itself), to be on.

    A2

  39. 539
    kesinadjective

    certain, sure; definite, exact; definitely

    Henüz kesin değil, yarın söylerim.

    It's not certain yet, I'll tell you tomorrow.

    Kesinlikle = definitely, absolutely. In casual speech kesin alone also means surely: Kesin unuttu (He must have forgotten).

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 9: Conditionals

  40. 540
    sistemnoun

    system

    Sistem çöktü, biraz bekleyin.

    The system has crashed, please wait a little.

    As in English: eğitim sistemi (the education system).

    A2

  41. 541
    teklifnoun

    offer; proposal; suggestion

    Güzel bir iş teklifi aldım.

    I got a nice job offer.

    Teklif etmek = to offer, to propose; evlenme teklifi = marriage proposal.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 4: Noun clauses

  42. 542
    müziknoun

    music

    Yemek yaparken müzik dinlerim.

    I listen to music while I cook.

    accusative müziği

    The k becomes ğ before a vowel: müziği. Müzik dinlemek = to listen to music.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 6: The present continuous

  43. 543
    yaklaşmakverb

    to approach, to come near; to be nearly (a time)

    Yaklaşma, köpek ısırır!

    Don't come closer, the dog bites!

    aorist yaklaşır · present yaklaşıyor · past yaklaştı · future yaklaşacak

    From yakın (near); the goal takes the dative: Bana yaklaşma. Saat beşe yaklaşıyor = It's nearly five.

    B1

  44. 544
    ananoun

    mother; main, principal

    Ana dilim Türkçe.

    My mother tongue is Turkish.

    Anne is the everyday word for mom; ana sounds old-fashioned, but lives on in compounds: ana dili (mother tongue), ana yol (main road), ana cadde (main street).

    A2

  45. 545
    yaşlıadjective

    old, elderly (of people)

    Otobüste yaşlı bir kadına yer verdim.

    I gave my seat to an old woman on the bus.

    For people and animals; old things are eski. Yaşlılar = the elderly.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 4: Questions and negation

  46. 546
    yavaşadjective

    slow; slowly; quiet, soft (of a voice)

    Daha yavaş konuşur musunuz, lütfen?

    Could you speak more slowly, please?

    Also an adverb. Yavaş yavaş = little by little; Yavaş ol! = Take it easy!

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 12: Requests and company

  47. 547
    beyaznoun

    white

    Beyaz gömleğimi gördün mü?

    Have you seen my white shirt?

    Like the other colours, a noun and an adjective: beyaz bir araba, Beyaz sana yakışıyor (White suits you).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 2: Vowel harmony and plurals

  48. 548
    böyleceadverb

    thus, in this way; so, so that

    Erken çıktık, böylece trafiğe takılmadık.

    We left early, so we didn't get stuck in traffic.

    From böyle (like this): it introduces the result of what was just said.

    B1

  49. 549
    acabaadverb

    I wonder; (softens a question)

    Acaba yarın hava nasıl olacak?

    I wonder what the weather will be like tomorrow.

    Turns a question into I wonder: Acaba gelir mi? (I wonder if she'll come). It is not a question word itself.

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 9: Conditionals

  50. 550
    yüksekadjective

    high; tall (buildings, mountains); loud

    Müziğin sesi çok yüksek, kısar mısın?

    The music is too loud, could you turn it down?

    Yüksek sesle = out loud, loudly. Tall people are uzun boylu, not yüksek.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 8: Comparing

  51. 551
    uygunadjective

    suitable, appropriate; convenient; reasonable (of a price)

    Yarın sizin için uygun mu?

    Does tomorrow work for you?

    Uygun fiyat = a reasonable price. What it suits takes the dative: çocuklara uygun (suitable for children).

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 7: Stacked voices

  52. 552
    sürekliadverb

    constantly, all the time; continuous, permanent

    Telefonu sürekli çalıyor.

    Her phone rings all the time.

    From sürmek (to last). As an adjective: sürekli iş (a permanent job).

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 6: Compound verbs

  53. 553
    terk etmekverb

    to leave, to abandon; to quit

    Beni terk etme, lütfen.

    Please don't leave me.

    aorist terk eder · present terk ediyor · past terk etti · future terk edecek

    Stronger than bırakmak or ayrılmak: to leave for good. What you leave takes the accusative: evi terk etmek.

    C1First taught in C1 · Unit 1: Stacked modality

  54. 554
    tuhafadjective

    strange, odd, weird; funny (peculiar)

    Bugün çok tuhaf davranıyorsun.

    You're acting really weird today.

    Close to garip. Tuhafıma gitti = It struck me as odd.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 2: As if

  55. 555
    aynenadverb

    exactly, just so; exactly as, just as it is

    Aynen öyle, çok haklısın.

    Exactly, you're absolutely right.

    In casual speech, a one-word Exactly! to agree. Also exactly as: Aynen böyle yap (Do it just like this).

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 9: Everyday colloquial Turkish

  56. 556
    ajannoun

    (secret) agent; spy

    Bu filmdeki ajan çok komik.

    The agent in this movie is really funny.

    A spy, mostly in films. A sales agent is temsilci; a real estate agent, emlakçı.

    B1

  57. 557
    cesetnoun

    (dead) body, corpse

    Polis nehirde bir ceset buldu.

    The police found a body in the river.

    accusative cesedi

    The t becomes d before a vowel: cesedi. Only a dead body; the living body is vücut.

    B1

  58. 558
    korkunçadjective

    terrible, awful; frightening, horrible

    Korkunç bir rüya gördüm.

    I had a terrible dream.

    From korku (fear). Like awful, it can just mean very bad: Hava korkunç (The weather is awful).

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 1: Past continuous and pluperfect

  59. 559
    koşmakverb

    to run; to rush

    Her sabah parkta koşarım.

    I run in the park every morning.

    aorist koşar · present koşuyor · past koştu · future koşacak

    Koşu = running, a run. Also to rush somewhere: Hemen eve koştum.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 4: Habits and truths: the aorist

  60. 560
    uçaknoun

    plane, airplane

    Uçağımız saat üçte kalkıyor.

    Our plane leaves at three.

    accusative uçağı

    From uçmak (to fly). The k becomes ğ before a vowel: uçağı. Uçakla = by plane.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 12: Requests and company

  61. 561
    kurbannoun

    victim; sacrifice

    Polis kurbanın adını açıklamadı.

    The police didn't release the victim's name.

    Kurban Bayramı = the Feast of the Sacrifice. Kazaya kurban gitmek = to die in an accident.

    B1

  62. 562
    ofisnoun

    office

    Bugün ofiste değilim, evden çalışıyorum.

    I'm not in the office today, I'm working from home.

    A workplace; büro means the same. Front-vowel suffixes: ofiste.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 5: Where things are

  63. 563
    güle gülephrase

    goodbye (said to the person leaving)

    Güle güle, yine bekleriz!

    Goodbye, come again!

    Said by the person staying; the one leaving says hoşça kal. Güle güle kullan = Enjoy it (something new).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 1: Letters and sounds

  64. 564
    saçnoun

    hair (on the head)

    Saçların çok güzel olmuş!

    Your hair looks really nice!

    Singular or plural: saçım or saçlarım. Body hair is kıl or tüy.

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 3: Hearsay and inference

  65. 565
    sokaknoun

    street; outside (sokakta: out, in the street)

    Çocuklar sokakta oynuyor.

    The kids are playing in the street.

    accusative sokağı

    The k becomes ğ before a vowel: sokağı. Smaller than a cadde (avenue). Sokağa çıkmak = to go out.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 7: To and from

  66. 566
    doğmakverb

    to be born; to rise (the sun)

    1995'te İzmir'de doğdum.

    I was born in Izmir in 1995.

    aorist doğar · present doğuyor · past doğdu · future doğacak

    Active in Turkish: doğdum (I was born). Also of the sun: Güneş doğuyor. Doğum günü = birthday.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 1: The past tense

  67. 567
    kazanoun

    accident

    Yolda bir kaza oldu, trafik durdu.

    There was an accident on the road and traffic stopped.

    Kaza yapmak = to have an accident (as the driver); kaza geçirmek = to be in an accident.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 7: Let's: suggestions and wishes

  68. 568
    mümkünadjective

    possible

    Bu mümkün değil.

    That's not possible.

    Mümkün olduğunca = as much as possible. İmkânsız = impossible.

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 9: Conditionals

  69. 569
    çözmekverb

    to solve; to untie, to undo

    Bu sorunu birlikte çözeriz.

    We'll solve this problem together.

    aorist çözer · present çözüyor · past çözdü · future çözecek

    Çözüm = solution. Also to untie: düğümü çözmek (to untie the knot).

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 7: Stacked voices

  70. 570
    yeterinceadverb

    enough, sufficiently

    Yeterince uyumadım, çok yorgunum.

    I didn't get enough sleep, I'm really tired.

    From yeter (enough) + -CA. The adjective is yeterli (enough, sufficient).

    B1

  71. 571
    masanoun

    table; desk

    Masayı pencerenin yanına koyalım.

    Let's put the table by the window.

    Also a desk: çalışma masası. Setting the table is sofrayı kurmak.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 2: Vowel harmony and plurals

  72. 572
    avukatnoun

    lawyer

    Avukatım yarın sizi arayacak.

    My lawyer will call you tomorrow.

    The t doesn't soften: avukatı. Avukat tutmak = to hire a lawyer.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 3: Saying who you are

  73. 573
    kapamakverb

    to close, to shut; to turn off; to hang up (the phone)

    Kapıyı kapa, çok soğuk.

    Shut the door, it's very cold.

    aorist kapar · present kapıyor · past kapadı · future kapayacak

    Same as kapatmak, which is more common in speech. The a becomes ı before -(I)yor: kapıyor.

    A2

  74. 574
    hayvannoun

    animal

    Evde hayvan besliyor musunuz?

    Do you have any pets?

    Hayvan beslemek = to keep a pet; evcil hayvan = pet; hayvanat bahçesi = zoo.

    A1

  75. 575
    yıldıznoun

    star

    Bu gece gökyüzünde çok yıldız var.

    There are lots of stars in the sky tonight.

    Also a film star, and a hotel's stars: beş yıldızlı otel.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 9: Everyday colloquial Turkish

  76. 576
    günaydıninterjection

    good morning

    Günaydın! İyi uyudun mu?

    Good morning! Did you sleep well?

    Until about noon; after that, iyi günler or merhaba.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 1: Letters and sounds

  77. 577
    ortaknoun

    partner (in business); common, shared, joint

    Ortağım yarın İzmir'den dönüyor.

    My business partner is back from Izmir tomorrow.

    accusative ortağı

    The k becomes ğ before a vowel: ortağı. As an adjective: ortak bir arkadaşımız (a mutual friend of ours).

    B1

  78. 578
    rahatsızadjective

    uncomfortable; unwell, ill; disturbed, bothered

    Bu ayakkabılar çok rahatsız.

    These shoes are really uncomfortable.

    Rahatsız etmek = to disturb, to bother: Rahatsız etmeyin (Do not disturb). Biraz rahatsızım = I'm not feeling well.

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 12: Reported speech

  79. 579
    kuralnoun

    rule

    Oyunun kurallarını biliyor musun?

    Do you know the rules of the game?

    Kurala uymak = to follow a rule. Back-vowel suffixes: kuralı.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 6: Must and need

  80. 580
    berbatadjective

    awful, terrible; ruined

    Hava berbat, evde kalalım.

    The weather's awful, let's stay in.

    Colloquial and strong. Berbat etmek = to ruin, to mess up: Her şeyi berbat ettin!

    A2

  81. 581
    ekipnoun

    team, crew

    Yeni ekibimiz çok iyi.

    Our new team is very good.

    accusative ekibi

    The p becomes b before a vowel: ekibi. A team at work or a film crew; a sports team is usually takım.

    B1

  82. 582
    kahvenoun

    coffee; coffeehouse

    Bir Türk kahvesi, lütfen. Orta şekerli.

    A Turkish coffee, please. Medium sweet.

    Türk kahvesi comes sade (no sugar), orta or şekerli. Kahvaltı (breakfast) comes from kahve altı.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 6: The present continuous

  83. 583
    âşıkadjective

    in love; lover; folk minstrel

    Sana âşık oldum.

    I've fallen in love with you.

    Written with â, unlike aşık (knucklebone). Who you love takes the dative: Sana âşığım.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 10: As long as, unless, in case

  84. 584
    büyümekverb

    to grow (up); to get bigger

    İzmir'de doğdum ama Ankara'da büyüdüm.

    I was born in Izmir but grew up in Ankara.

    aorist büyür · present büyüyor · past büyüdü · future büyüyecek

    From büyük (big). Büyütmek = to raise (a child), to enlarge.

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 2: Used to, was going to, should have

  85. 585
    suçlamakverb

    to accuse; to blame

    Beni suçlama, ben bir şey yapmadım!

    Don't blame me, I didn't do anything!

    aorist suçlar · present suçluyor · past suçladı · future suçlayacak

    From suç (crime, fault). The a becomes u before -(I)yor: suçluyor. Hırsızlıkla suçlamak = to accuse of theft.

    B1

  86. 586
    belliadjective

    clear, obvious; certain, particular

    Belli ki çok yorgunsun.

    You're obviously very tired.

    Belli ki = obviously; Belli olmaz = You never know; belli bir saat = a certain time.

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 3: Hearsay and inference

  87. 587
    pisliknoun

    dirt, filth, mess; scumbag (rude)

    Bu ne pislik! Hemen temizle.

    What a mess! Clean it up right away.

    accusative pisliği

    From pis (dirty); the k becomes ğ before a vowel: pisliği. Said of a person, it is a strong insult.

    B1

  88. 588
    araştırmakverb

    to research, to look into; to investigate; to search

    Bu konuyu internette araştırdım.

    I looked into this topic online.

    aorist araştırır · present araştırıyor · past araştırdı · future araştıracak

    Araştırma = research. Compare aramak (to look for).

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 5: Formal Turkish

  89. 589
    meselenoun

    matter, issue; problem

    Mesele para değil, zaman.

    The issue isn't money, it's time.

    Mesele değil = It's no big deal. Close to sorun and konu.

    B1

  90. 590
    çevirmekverb

    to translate; to turn (round); to dial

    Bu mektubu İngilizceye çevirir misin?

    Could you translate this letter into English?

    aorist çevirir · present çeviriyor · past çevirdi · future çevirecek

    The language takes the dative: Türkçeye çevirmek. Also to turn: Sayfayı çevir (Turn the page). Çeviri = translation.

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 12: Reported speech

  91. 591
    dikkatliadjective

    careful; carefully

    Dikkatli ol, yol buzlu.

    Be careful, the road is icy.

    Dikkat + -lI. Dikkatli sür = Drive carefully. The opposite is dikkatsiz.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 8: Comparing

  92. 592
    kayıpnoun

    loss; missing, lost

    Kayıp eşya bürosu nerede?

    Where's the lost and found?

    accusative kaybı

    The ı drops and the p becomes b before a vowel: kaybı. Kaybolmak = to get lost; kaybetmek = to lose.

    B1

  93. 593
    ağlamakverb

    to cry, to weep

    Bebek bütün gece ağladı.

    The baby cried all night.

    aorist ağlar · present ağlıyor · past ağladı · future ağlayacak

    The a becomes ı before -(I)yor: ağlıyor. Ağlama! = Don't cry!

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 8: Converbs II: the more, whenever, because

  94. 594
    bayılmakverb

    to love, to be crazy about; to faint

    Türk kahvesine bayılırım!

    I love Turkish coffee!

    aorist bayılır · present bayılıyor · past bayıldı · future bayılacak

    With the dative, a strong to love: Bu şarkıya bayılıyorum. Literally to faint: Sıcaktan bayıldı.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 2: As if

  95. 595
    nefesnoun

    breath

    Derin bir nefes al.

    Take a deep breath.

    Nefes almak = to breathe (in); nefes nefese = out of breath.

    A2

  96. 596
    parmaknoun

    finger; toe (ayak parmağı)

    Parmağımı kestim, yara bandı var mı?

    I cut my finger, is there a bandage?

    accusative parmağı

    The k becomes ğ before a vowel: parmağı. A toe is ayak parmağı.

    A1

  97. 597
    dayanmakverb

    to bear, to stand, to put up with; to lean (on); to be based on

    Bu sıcağa dayanamıyorum!

    I can't stand this heat!

    aorist dayanır · present dayanıyor · past dayandı · future dayanacak

    With the dative: acıya dayanmak (to bear pain). Also to lean: duvara dayanmak.

    B1

  98. 598
    milletnoun

    nation, people; everyone, folks (casual)

    Millet nerede? Herkes gitmiş mi?

    Where is everyone? Has everybody left?

    Formally a nation: Türk milleti. In speech, everyone, people: Millet ne der? (What will people say?)

    B1

  99. 599
    özlemekverb

    to miss (someone or something); to long for

    Seni çok özledim!

    I missed you so much!

    aorist özler · present özlüyor · past özledi · future özleyecek

    The e becomes ü before -(I)yor: özlüyor. I miss you is usually in the past: Seni özledim.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 8: Definite objects

  100. 600
    anahtarnoun

    key

    Anahtarımı bulamıyorum.

    Anahtarlık = key ring. Anahtar kelime = keyword.

About this list

The words are ranked by how often they come up in film and TV dialogue, so the list leans towards spoken Turkish. Words are listed in their dictionary form (verbs in the infinitive, gelmek), names and fragments are left out, and ranks are estimates rather than exact counts.

The order of the list is adapted from the 2018 Turkish list of FrequencyWords by Hermit Dave, made from the OpenSubtitles2018 corpus via OPUS, and is licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0. The meanings, example sentences and notes are original to Daily Turkish.
